01 / About

Engineering clarity into complex systems.

My work sits where software meets physical systems. Through my undergraduate thesis, I develop autonomous navigation for unmanned surface vehicles using Lazy Theta Star for global planning and SAPF-DDPG for adaptive local obstacle avoidance.

I enjoy algorithmic problem-solving, simulation-based analysis, and turning technical concepts into implementations that can be clearly explained, tested, and used.

03 / Selected projects

Work grounded in real problems.

01Undergraduate thesisJan — Jul 2026

USV Path Planning using Lazy Theta Star & SAPF-DDPG

Combined global path planning with adaptive local avoidance for autonomous USV navigation. The system uses a 4-DOF model, static and dynamic obstacle scenarios, G2 Continuous Bézier Spiral smoothing, and DDPG-tuned SAPF parameters, evaluated in simulation and on the LSS-01 platform.
